history.summary: IDENTITY: Nutan Kalibari ('Nutan' = 'new' in Bengali) is a Kali temple in Kailashahar, Bhadrakali area, documented by indiano.travel (gigantic entrance gate, many decorated idols, noted for night lighting) and a 2018 Tripadvisor review of the Kali Bari temple at Kailashahar. The Kailashahar Wikipedia page lists a 'New Kali temple' among the town's notable religious sites alongside the Lakshmi Narayan temple - almost certainly this same shrine. No founding date or history is published ('the place doesn't have any remarkable history' per indiano.travel). POSSIBLE OVERLAP FLAG: seq 1039 (id kali-temple-kailashahar) provisionally used Wikipedia's 'New Kali temple' as its best-supported referent with high uncertainty and different coordinates; treated here as its own record pending confirmation. LOCATION FLAG: coordinates are town-level and approximate - the exact shrine coordinates are unverified, and the plus code published by indiano.travel (8XGX+FJ8) decodes outside Kailashahar and was discarded as unreliable.

name: Nutan Kalibari, Kailashahar
town_description: Kailashahar is the headquarters town of Unakoti district in northern Tripura, on the banks of the Manu river near the Bangladesh border. It is known for the ancient Unakoti rock-cut Shaivite shrines nearby, the Lakshmi Narayan temple, and a mixed Bengali-tribal culture.

travel.airport: Maharaja Bir Bikram Airport, Agartala (~180 km by road; verify)
travel.railway: No station in Kailashahar; nearest major station Dharmanagar (~30 km, verify)
travel.road: Bhadrakali area of Kailashahar town; local autos and taxis

visitor_information.best_time: October-March; Dusshera/Durga Puja period is the most festive
visitor_information.opening_hours: Reported open 24 hours, 7 days, no entry fee (single source - verify locally)
